title: Four test gaps the irc-verbs review found
description:
Found by the test review of branch irc-verbs. None is a defect in
shipped behaviour; each is a test that does not cover what it looks like
it covers. Grouped because they are all small and in the same area.

1. The rehash `*` branch has no end-to-end case.
   config_file_param is unit-tested for every grammar class it refuses
   and for the length bound, but nothing drives a daemon whose
   configuration path cannot be written as a middle parameter, so the
   extra NOTICE ("REHASH: the configuration file is <path>") and the 382
   that then carries `*` are never exercised together. config_at already
   takes the directory, so one test with a file named `my agent.toml`
   covers both, and pins the order of the two lines, which nothing else
   does. (crates/mimid-agent/tests/rehash.rs)

2. a_config_file_over_the_limit_is_refused litters the shared temp
   directory. It writes its 256 KiB fixture to
   std::env::temp_dir()/mimid-config-limit-<pid> and removes it only on
   the success path, so a failure or panic leaves it, and two runs that
   land on the same pid share a path. Two leftovers were on this machine
   when the review ran (/data/tmp/mimid-config-limit-861235 held the
   262145-octet agent.toml). Every other test in the crate uses
   tempfile::tempdir(), already a dev-dependency, which cleans up on
   unwind and cannot collide. Worth doing: the disk filled during this
   epic's gate run. (crates/mimid-agent/src/config.rs, tests module)

3. refresh_clients's normalization is the one behaviour its doc comment
   singles out and the one not covered. The test uses only URIs already
   in RFC 3986 normal form, so deleting both normalized_uri calls leaves
   the whole workspace passing. Insert a Person whose user differs from
   the leaf's credential URI only in a percent-encoding or case that
   normalizes away, and assert its clients still counts: same test, one
   extra record. (mimid-agent-store tests/groundwork.rs
   a_person_record_counts_the_clients_in_a_shared_group; see bead
   mimid-1wgh.147, which is the same function's other half)

4. monitor_answers_the_list_and_its_bound claims more than it shows.
   Its comment says "L lists what was asked for, as it was asked for"
   and it asserts 732 carries alice-a,mimid,nobody-x -- but the list is a
   BTreeMap keyed by the folded nick, and for those three targets the
   folded order and the insertion order coincide, so nothing about order
   is tested. The companion test confirms it: after MONITOR + n0..n99 it
   checks only the length, because the real output is n0,n1,n10,...,n99,n9.
   The spec fixes no order, so the code is right; either reword the
   comment to say the list echoes each target's spelling (which the
   BOB-A/MIMID case does prove) and that the order is the folded one, or
   pick three targets whose folded order differs from the order sent.
   (crates/mimid-agent/tests/irc.rs)
